segments.title: Chương 294: 0296
segments.content:
Bian Guanyue just wanted to come to Chen Guiliang's house for a visit; she really didn't have the nerve to stay over at the Chen's for the New Year.

She arrived on the evening of the 28th of the twelfth lunar month and planned to leave after lunch on the 29th, to spend the Spring Festival at her maternal grandparents' home in the county town.

When Bian Guanyue was leaving, Grandma was the most reluctant to see her go, holding her hand and talking nonstop.

"Come visit often whenever you have a break in the future," Grandma said.

Bian Guanyue nodded. "Yes, I'll come often."

Grandma said a few more words, then went back into the house and brought out a Yuan Shikai silver dollar, pressing it into Bian Guanyue's hand. "I don't have many old things, this is all that's left. You must keep it safe, don't ever lose it."

Bian Guanyue realized what it was, feeling both delighted and touched. "Thank you, Grandma."

The whole family walked them to the village road across the mountain hollow, where Yang Shuo had already been waiting in his car for a long time.

After getting in the car, Bian Guanyue kept waving.

It wasn't until they left the village that Chen Guiliang explained, "Grandma's family had four sisters and no brothers. When they got married, each of them was secretly given four silver dollars as part of their dowry. Silver dollars can be used to 'draw out wind,' which is a kind of folk remedy. Grandma's four silver dollars were borrowed by villagers to treat their children's 'wind,' and after being passed around, this is the only one left."

This was more precious than Bian Guanyue had guessed. She took out the silver dollar in surprise. "Isn't this the only dowry item Grandma has left?"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang nodded. "And now she's given it to you. Grandma likes you a lot."

Bian Guanyue's nose tingled. She thought of her own deceased paternal grandmother and said in a low voice, "Then how about I come visit Grandma every winter and summer break?"

Chen Guiliang smiled. "That would be great. If I'm not free then, you can come home to visit on my behalf."

"It's a deal then," Bian Guanyue said, wiping the corner of her eye with her finger.

After dropping Bian Guanyue off in the county town, Chen Guiliang went to her grandparents' house and sat for a while. He still had to set off back to the village in the mid-afternoon, as the big New Year's Eve dinner had to be eaten at his own home.

Some songs became huge hits because of the Spring Festival Gala, and their ringtones sold like crazy.

Even though Chen Guiliang could predict this, it was still very difficult to get the copyrights. For example, Ah Niu's "Peach Blossoms Blooming," the copyright belonged to Rock Records, but Rock Records had its own Rock Mobile company. They operated their own digital music business.

Chen Guiliang had only managed to send someone to secure the rights to one song in advance, "Invisible Wings."

Both songs were released in January 2006, but the SP service copyright for "Peach Blossoms Blooming" was surprisingly harder to acquire than that of "Invisible Wings." Isn't that counterintuitive?

Because the record companies they belonged to were different!

Angela Chang's Linfair Records was an independent record company in Taiwan and didn't place much importance on the SP service market in the mainland. As long as the price was high enough, they were willing to sell the rights to any song.

The language-based programs on this year's Spring Festival Gala were somewhat inferior compared to last year's.

They only produced a few classic lines: "A rooster that lays eggs, the fighter jet of roosters. Oh yeah!"

New Year's Day was spent at his own home.

From New Year's Eve to New Year's Day, Chen Guiliang spent a lot of time sending and receiving New Year's text messages. People he knew, people he didn't know, there was no telling how many people sent him text messages with their blessings.

On the second day of the new year, he went to visit his maternal grandmother's family.

Both his maternal grandfather and grandmother were quite robust. His youngest maternal uncle's widow wife was also several months pregnant.

On the third day, he went to his father's maternal grandmother's home.

He even ran into his younger female cousin, Zhang Qing (his paternal aunt's daughter).

When his cousin was little, her mother would drop her off at Chen Guiliang's house every winter and summer break for Grandma to look after. Chen Guiliang would play with his cousin and his younger male cousin, climbing trees in the mountains and catching fish in the river. The three of them had a very close relationship.

"You're about to take the college entrance exam, right?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Zhang Qing's personality was very introverted and shy. "The gaokao is this year."

"What kind of university do you think you can get into?" Chen Guiliang asked, knowing the answer.

Zhang Qing said, "A Third-Tier university."

For over twenty consecutive years, Sichuan province's acceptance rate for bachelor's degree programs ranked last in the country. The four perennially complaining provinces of Shanxi, Henan, Shandong, and Hebei actually had bachelor's acceptance rates that could trounce Sichuan's.

For kids here, getting into a Third-Tier university was already pretty good.

The competition was fierce.

But at this time, Third-Tier universities were basically private colleges affiliated with public universities. The tuition was ridiculously expensive; the cheaper ones were nearly ten thousand yuan, and the normal ones were twelve or thirteen thousand.

If Chen Guiliang didn't intervene, even if his cousin Zhang Qing got into a Third-Tier university, she would choose a junior college instead because her family couldn't afford it.

Chen Guiliang called Zhang Qing aside and said privately, "If you get into a Third-Tier university, call me if you don't have enough for tuition. Don't tell anyone about this."

Zhang Qing lowered her head and replied, "Okay."

Chen Guiliang was speechless. "You were quite mischievous as a child, how come you're becoming more and more introverted? Raise your head when you speak."

Zhang Qing obediently raised her head.

Chen Guiliang instructed, "In this last half year, work a little harder, try to get into a Second-Tier university."

"I'm very dumb," Zhang Qing said.

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm not your parent, don't use that line on me. Whether you've paid attention in class, whether you've reviewed and done your homework seriously afterward, you know these things clearly in your heart."

Zhang Qing was embarrassed by his words and finally became lively again, sticking her tongue out at Chen Guiliang playfully.

"That's more like it. Head down all day, not saying a word, as gloomy as a widowed daughter-in-law," Chen Guiliang laughed too.

Grandma's four sisters all brought their entire families to Great-Grandma's house for a New Year's gathering.

Four families, four generations under one roof, totaling more than twenty people.

Chen Guiliang was naturally the center of attention, but he had become so successful that it created a sense of unbridgeable distance.

His cousin-uncle, Feng Tao, was much more down-to-earth.

Feng Tao had completely taken over Tao Chenggang's computer shop and had moved it to the newly built digital plaza. Although he couldn't compare to a big boss, in the eyes of ordinary people, he was already a successful person.

His apprentice was from the next village over and had now become an old hand himself, managing the two new apprentices at the shop. His salary had naturally increased as well.

After lunch, the apprentice was even brought over by his parents, carrying gifts to thank Feng Tao for his guidance.

Great-Grandma, who was almost 90, was in increasingly poor health; now even walking was difficult. She sat in a chair sunbathing, watching her four daughters, sons-in-law, and their descendants play cards and chat.

Occasionally, when a child ran past playing, Great-Grandma would call them over and pull out a few pieces of candy to stuff into their hands.

Chen Guiliang also moved a small stool over to chat with Great-Grandma. "Great-Grandma, how many bowls of rice can you eat these days?"

Although Great-Grandma's body was weak, her hearing was fine. "My appetite isn't good. I used to eat one bowl, but last year I could only manage half a bowl. The coffin in the house has been sitting there for over ten years; it should get some use in the next couple of years."

The elderly woman was not afraid of death. More than ten years ago, Great-Grandma had felt that she was about to die.

So she had a coffin and burial clothes custom-made for herself and had a beautiful memorial portrait taken. The coffin sat in her storeroom, and the portrait had been hanging on the wall all along. From time to time, she would even take out the burial clothes and try them on.

Every extra day she lived, she felt she had earned.

She ended up living for more than a decade longer, and without suffering from any major illnesses.

Great-Grandma felt she was very blessed.

Great-Grandma said, "Last Qingming Festival, I had your cousin-uncle carry me on his back to look at a plot of land. It's halfway up the mountain in Wanjia'ao. The feng shui there is very good, I've always liked it. Your Third Great-Aunt-Uncle has connections and has already talked it over with the village party secretary. After I die, I'll be buried there. If you have time, come visit my grave. But don't let it interfere with your work; if you're busy, don't come back."

"I'll come back every year to visit your grave," Chen Guiliang said with a grin.

The expressions, tones, and content of their conversation seemed odd, yet also strangely warm.

When Chen Guiliang was not yet a month old, he fell seriously ill and needed more than 20 yuan for hospitalization fees.

At that time, his mother held him and waited at the hospital while his father and grandmother went around trying to borrow money. Even the city relatives on his father's stepfather's side wouldn't lend them money. In the end, it was his father who went to Great-Grandma's and got the money.

Without Great-Grandma, Chen Guiliang probably wouldn't have lived to be a month old.

Great-Grandma suddenly got interested and had Chen Guiliang help her into the house to see the coffin.

She seriously described the specifications and materials of her coffin and even rummaged inside to pull out a few coffin nails. Then she joyfully changed into her burial clothes, sat smiling beside the coffin, and asked Chen Guiliang to take a picture of her as a memento.

On New Year's Day of all times...

Great-Grandma had opened up and was talking more and more. "The country promotes cremation now. I'm letting the government down, I want an improper burial. When the mourning hall is set up, remember to come back and play cards."

Chen Guiliang promised, "Alright. When the time comes, I'll come back, play cards with Guirong and the others, and keep vigil for you. And I'll win their money."
